content.text: The text reviews diseases of the rectum, anus, and intestinal tract, including congenital malformations, prolapse, polyps, hemorrhoids, strictures, proctitis, fissures, ulcers, abscesses, fistulae, syphilis, tuberculosis, cancer, neurological dysfunction, and treatment approaches. It also describes intestinal parasites—tapeworms, flukes, nematodes, trichinae, and filariae—their life cycles, symptoms, transmission, treatment, and prevention. Major preventive advice includes thoroughly cooking meat, filtering or boiling water, maintaining hygiene, and avoiding contaminated food and close contact with infected animals. The final section introduces liver disorders such as biliousness, lithaemia, temporary glycosuria, and jaundice, emphasizing diet, exercise, digestive dysfunction, and biliary obstruction.
